title: GWAYA-gated rejection-sampling fine-tuning (RFT) of a low-cost coding assistant that trains and runs in under 8 GB of VRAM
requested_by: the user, 2026-10-24: implement the training and leverage GWAYA as a low-cost, efficient coding assistant on a GPU of less than 8 GB VRAM
roadmap: HM-S10-06 (coding curriculum for the campaign), the GWAYA entry of ROADMAP 3.8; new task HM-S10-11
what_gwaya_is_here: GWAYA (xaviercallens/GWAYA-GwenLayaOpenModel, MIT) is a fail-closed verification layer: a candidate is accepted only if a zero-stub AST audit is clean AND an oracle (sandboxed execution of the task tests) passes, otherwise UNVERIFIED. It trains nothing. E15 adds the training around it: GWAYA decides which model-generated solutions become training data and which inference-time candidate is returned.
deviations_from_gwaya: GWAYA own Bubblewrap oracle is not available on this host (bwrap not installed); the sandbox is a user/mount/net/pid-namespace launcher with tmpfs over the home directory, rlimits and an empty environment, tested with hostile probes; it is NOT equivalent to GWAYA own oracle and the gate is reported as GWAYA-style

only gwaya/ast_audit.py is used, vendored unmodified at a pinned commit (third_party/gwaya/PROVENANCE.md); the gwaya package, its MCP server and its repair prompts are not used; the repair loop here is our own and documented
Laya (the Convai decision model / the Laya-LoRA companion) is a gate classifier, not a code generator, and is not used

model.base: Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct (the model of GWAYA own README evaluation), fp16 weights, no quantisation library
model.lora: hand-rolled, rank 16, alpha 32, PEFT-scale init, on q,k,v,o,gate,up,down of every layer; fp32 LoRA parameters and optimizer states, fp16 autocast, static loss scale 256
model.vram_cap: torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(7.5 GiB / total) at process start, so that every stage must run inside an 8 GB card budget even though the T4 has 15 GB; peak reserved per stage is recorded

data.train: MBPP full train + validation (task_ids 511-974, 464 problems), used only for rejection sampling and fine-tuning
data.eval: MBPP sanitized test (257 problems; task_ids disjoint from train, asserted) and HumanEval (164; evaluation only, never trained on)
data.prompting: chat prompt with the problem text and the VISIBLE test test_list[0]; the inference gate sees only test_list[0]; final pass@1 uses ALL tests; the RFT gate uses all tests of the train problem

procedure.C1: base + GWAYA inference loop: candidates [greedy, 2 samples T=0.7 top_p=0.95], first gate-passing (stub audit + visible test) wins, else up to 3 repair rounds with the gate feedback, else the first greedy candidate
procedure.RFT_generation: 8 samples per train problem (T=0.8, top_p=0.95), gate with all tests, keep at most 2 distinct (AST-normalised) accepted solutions per problem
procedure.training: 3 epochs, lr 2e-4 cosine, 10 warmup steps, micro-batch 4 x accumulation 4, max sequence 768, gradient checkpointing, loss on assistant tokens only

hypotheses.H15a: RFT improves greedy pass@1 on MBPP-sanitized: C2 - C0 >= +3.0 points with exact two-sided McNemar p < 0.05 -> supported; C2 - C0 < 0 with p < 0.05 -> refuted (fine-tuning hurts); otherwise inconclusive
hypotheses.H15b: the GWAYA inference loop improves the base: C1 - C0 >= +5.0 points with McNemar p < 0.05 -> supported; C1 - C0 <= 0 -> refuted; otherwise inconclusive (GWAYA own README reports +4.7 to +7.8 points for the same model family and fails its own +8.0 gate; +5.0 is chosen before any run)
hypotheses.H15c: stacking (descriptive): C3 - C1 and C3 - C0 with McNemar p, no status
hypotheses.H15d: resource: training and every inference stage run to completion with the 7.5 GiB cap enforced (peak reserved <= 8.0 GiB) -> supported; an out-of-memory under the cap -> refuted
hypotheses.H15e_generalisation_descriptive: HumanEval C2 - C0 with McNemar p (does RFT on MBPP transfer or hurt out of distribution), no status

controls.gate_accepts_references: >= 95% of the MBPP reference solutions (code field) of 100 train problems and >= 98% of HumanEval canonical solutions are ACCEPTED by the gate
controls.stubs_rejected: 100% of planted stub bodies are rejected
controls.containment: the hostile-candidate probes of tests/test_e15_gate.py (secret file read, network, memory bomb, infinite loop, fork bomb, disk fill, host process inspection, tampering with the vendored auditor) are all contained; gate_available() true
controls.no_leakage: no eval task_id or normalised prompt in the training set
controls.run_is_valid_iff: all controls pass; otherwise H15a-H15e are reported as invalid

fail_fast: exit 3 if fewer than 150 of the 464 train problems yield >= 1 accepted sample (the rejection-sampled set would be too small to learn from); exit 3 if the projected total time exceeds --max-hours (default 3.0)
cost_accounting: generated tokens, GPU seconds, accepted solutions per GPU-minute, peak reserved GiB and an NVML power x time energy estimate (Wh) per stage; descriptive
decision_consequences: H15a and H15b supported: the pipeline (GWAYA gate + RFT + LoRA under 8 GB) is a documented low-cost recipe for the community GPU program and a candidate base for the coding curriculum of HM-S10-06; H15a not supported but H15b supported: the inference-time gate alone is the efficient path and training needs more verified data; neither supported: the recipe does not beat the base at this size and the result is reported as such
scope: one 1.5B model, one fine-tuning run (one seed, no interval over training seeds), MBPP-sanitized n=257 and HumanEval n=164, a sandbox that is not GWAYA own; pass@1 differences are paired by problem (McNemar) but do not include training-seed variance; no claim beyond Python function synthesis on these two benchmarks
non_monetary: no PTS or $HIVE reward is attached to any part of this experiment
